english-rose: Roses are related to apples, cherries and almonds — all members of the same plant family.
ixora-dwarf: Dwarf ixora is a butterfly magnet — its tubular flowers are built exactly for butterfly tongues.
colius-small: Coleus exists in hundreds of leaf patterns — no two varieties show the same colour combination.
thuja-vidya: Thuja is called the 'tree of life' — its resin, leaves and wood all have traditional medicinal uses.
lemon-grass-chai-patti: Lemongrass tea is a natural mosquito deterrent — the citral in the leaves is the same compound used in repellents.
dracena-dwarf: Dracaenas remove toxins from indoor air — they're among the most-studied houseplants for air cleaning.
jasmine-sambac-mogra: Mogra is India's most iconic garland flower — its scent intensifies at night, which is when it's picked.
croton-lemon: Croton's yellow spots are chlorophyll working around the variegation — a living patchwork of leaf chemistry.
spider-plant: Spider plants were among the first plants tested by NASA for cleaning indoor air — and they're safe for cats.
china-rose-desi-gudhal: Hibiscus flowers last just a day or two, but the plant blooms so relentlessly you'll hardly notice.
foxtail-asperegus: Foxtail fern isn't a fern at all — it's a relative of the edible asparagus on your plate.
golden-seedum: Sedum stores water in its leaves so efficiently that a fallen leaf can grow an entirely new plant.
english-evy: English ivy clings with tiny rootlets along its stems — it climbs walls without any support at all.
fittonia-hanging: Fittonia faints dramatically when thirsty — then perks up within hours of watering, a built-in watering reminder.
christmas-tree: Real conifers like this one can live for centuries — some of the world's oldest trees are nearly 5,000 years old.
